results.corrected_extracted: All 15 measures were compared as areas under the curve in a repeated-measures analysis, with planned comparisons of the combination against each drug alone, one set of comparisons per measure; every test with p below .05 (one tailed) was counted as significant, with no correction, justified by directional hypotheses from the authors' earlier study. The authors suggest cocaethylene may matter more for heart effects late in the session (4th paragraph), and say the findings point to an increased risk of organ ischaemia, infarction and arrhythmia (5th); the paper reports no heart events or rhythm findings, and no test separates an effect of cocaethylene from the rise in cocaine. Participants were chosen because they already used both drugs (6th paragraph); the authors say it is unclear whether people who use both drugs have a premorbid vulnerability to psychiatric disorders or whether the combination is more toxic to the central nervous system than cocaine alone (7th); they list the intranasal route as a limit, since smoked or injected cocaine might give larger effects (9th).
